Griffin used a theatrical company to conceal his invisibility. He wore bandages, dark glasses, a false nose, clothes and other coverings so that people would think he was an ordinary injured man.

The baker's furnace was essential because bread was a part of Goan daily life and tradition. Bread was needed at breakfast, festivals, marriages and other important occasions. The baker supplied loaves and sweet breads and his profession continued from generation to generation. The furnace therefore represented both food and livelihood. It was closely connected with the culture of the village.

Coorg is rich in forests and wildlife. Elephants, birds and other animals make the region attractive to visitors. The river, forests and hills also provide opportunities for trekking, rafting, canoeing and fishing. The natural beauty and adventure activities make animals and nature a great source of entertainment. Thus Coorg offers both peaceful and exciting experiences.

The poet gives humorous clues instead of ordinary descriptions. The lion roars, the Bengal tiger may eat a person, the leopard leaps, the bear hugs, the hyena appears to laugh and the crocodile sheds tears. The dangerous animals are presented in playful and exaggerated ways. These contrasts make identification funny. The poem turns a dangerous subject into entertaining verse.

Anne Gregory's beautiful hair attracts people, but the poem questions whether such attraction is true love. Physical beauty is temporary and can change. The poet says that human beings are attracted to outward beauty, whereas God alone can love a person for the inner self. The poem therefore gives greater importance to inner qualities than appearance. It teaches that genuine love should not depend only on physical beauty.

Bholi is initially timid because she has been neglected and mocked for her appearance and speech. Her teacher treats her with kindness and encourages her to speak and learn. Education gives Bholi confidence and self-respect. At the end she refuses to marry Bishamber when he demands dowry. Thus education changes her life and gives her the courage to make her own decision.

When Maxwell returned to London with Mij, people were curious about the strange animal and asked many questions. They made guesses about what Mij was and were puzzled by his appearance and behaviour. Maxwell patiently explained that Mij was an otter. OR Rajvir had studied the history, legends and cultivation of tea before visiting Assam. He knew about the Chinese legend, the Indian legend and the spread of tea cultivation. He also observed the vast green tea gardens closely and discussed them with Pranjol.

Source: 'From the Diary of Anne Frank' — Author: Anne Frank. Context: Anne is explaining to Mr Keesing why she talks so much. After being punished with an essay, she argues humorously that talking is a student's trait and that her talkativeness is partly inherited from her mother. The line shows Anne's wit and confidence.

Source: 'The Proposal' — Author: Anton Chekhov. Context: Lomov says this to Natalya during their quarrel. He tries to calm her and avoid further anger, but their discussion again turns into an argument. The polite address contrasts humorously with their constant quarrelling.

Source: 'Dust of Snow' — Poet: Robert Frost. Context: The poet's mood changes after a crow shakes snow from a hemlock tree onto him. The small incident saves part of a day that he had regretted. The lines express the positive effect of a simple experience.

Source: 'The Ball Poem' — Poet: John Berryman. Context: The poet describes a quiet moonlit night while the boy faces the loss of his ball. The peaceful setting contrasts with his sadness and helps convey the boy's first important lesson about loss and responsibility.

Lencho expected a good harvest because his crop was growing well. The hailstorm destroyed the entire crop and brought him despair. He wrote a letter to God asking for money. The postmaster collected money and sent it to preserve Lencho's faith. Lencho was happy to receive the envelope but became angry because it contained less money than he had requested. Thus expectation, apparent fulfilment and destruction followed one another.

The pilot began the flight happily because he was returning home and looked forward to breakfast with his family. The night sky was clear and the moon was shining. Soon a storm appeared and the aeroplane entered dark clouds. His compass and radio stopped working and he became lost. A mysterious black aeroplane appeared and guided him through the storm. After landing, he discovered that no other aeroplane had been seen, turning his pleasant flight into a mysterious and challenging experience.

The young seagull was afraid that his wings would not support him. His brothers and sister flew around him and called him, showing that flying was possible. His parents encouraged him but did not carry him. Finally his mother came near him with a piece of fish and moved away. Driven by hunger, he jumped and spread his wings. He discovered that he could fly and soon joined his family confidently.

Buddha taught that human life is temporary and is accompanied by suffering. Birth, old age, disease and death are unavoidable. Kisa Gotami learned this truth when she could not find a house untouched by death. She understood that death is common to all mortals. Buddha taught that attachment increases sorrow. Acceptance of the truth of mortality leads towards peace.

A tiger is naturally happier in a forest because it can move freely, hunt prey and live according to its instincts. In the zoo it is locked behind bars in a small cage. It walks angrily along the cage and cannot use its strength freely. At night it hears the patrolling cars instead of the sounds of the jungle. The poem therefore contrasts natural freedom with the misery of captivity.

The boy learns responsibility when he loses his ball. The ball is valuable not because of its price but because it carries his memories and feelings. A new ball cannot replace the experience attached to the lost one. The loss teaches him that possessions can disappear and that he must accept such losses. This is an important step towards maturity.

a) According to Dr. Ambedkar, the constitution is a fundamental document that defines the position and powers of the legislature, executive and judiciary and their relation to citizens. b) Its purpose is not merely to create the organs of the state but also to limit their authority so that tyranny and oppression are prevented.

Google – an online friend: Google is a useful online friend for students when it is used wisely. It helps us find information, meanings, maps, educational videos and reference material quickly. It allows students to explore subjects beyond the textbook. It can help us clarify difficult concepts and prepare projects. However, every website does not contain reliable information. Students should compare information with trusted sources and teachers. Excessive use can waste time and reduce concentration. Privacy and safe browsing are also important. Google should support learning, not replace books or teachers. Responsible use makes learning wider and faster. Therefore, Google can be a valuable online friend when used with care. OR Water pollution – A threat to life: Water is essential for human beings, animals and plants. Yet rivers, lakes and groundwater are polluted by sewage, industrial waste, plastic and chemicals. Polluted water spreads diseases and destroys aquatic life. It also makes clean drinking water scarce. We should treat sewage and industrial waste before releasing it. Plastic and other waste must never be dumped into water bodies. Farmers should use fertilisers and pesticides carefully. Rainwater harvesting and conservation can protect water resources. Communities should keep lakes and rivers clean. Schools can teach students about water protection. Governments must enforce pollution-control laws. Every citizen has a role in preventing water pollution. Protecting water today protects life and future generations.

Letter – Shailaja/Shamit, X Standard, Adarsha Vidyalaya, Kalaburgi to the Chief Engineer, GESCOM, Kalaburgi. Subject: Complaint regarding frequent evening power cuts. Sir/Madam, I am a student of Class X at Adarsha Vidyalaya, Kalaburgi. I wish to bring to your notice the frequent power cuts in the evening in our area. These interruptions seriously affect students because evening is an important time for study and homework. They also cause inconvenience to families and disturb regular activities. I request you to investigate the problem and arrange a regular power supply, especially during evening study hours. Kindly take necessary action at the earliest. Yours faithfully, Shailaja/Shamit. OR Letter – Vinay/Vinuta, X Std, St. Joseph High School, Hasan to Grandfather. Dear Grandfather, I am happy to invite you and grandmother to our Grand Parents’ Day programme. It will be held on 15 August 2025 at 10:00 a.m. in the school auditorium. Your presence will make the celebration special for me. I warmly request both of you to attend the programme and bless us. I look forward to seeing you. With love, Vinay/Vinuta.

grammar.1: The subject is 'girl' and the future statement is positive, so the negative question tag is 'won't she?'.
grammar.2: 'But' is the suitable conjunction because the two clauses express contrast.
grammar.3: After 'planned', the infinitive 'to explore' is correct.
grammar.5: 'Bravely' modifies the verb 'fought', so it is an adverb.
grammar.6: Death is given the human action of laying hands, so the figure is personification.
grammar.7: A group of crooks is a gang.
grammar.8: The noun form of propense is propensity.
grammar.9: The opposite of expand is contract.
grammar.10: The homophone of aloud is allowed.
grammar.11: In passive voice, the object becomes the subject: By whom was the snake killed?
grammar.12: An exclamatory sentence can be changed into an assertive sentence without changing its meaning: Priya manages her house very wonderfully.
grammar.13: Use 'too + adjective + to-infinitive': Pranav is too short to play Basketball.
grammar.28: A yes/no question in reported speech uses whether/if and statement word order.
grammar.29: The comparative sentence becomes 'No other boy in the class is as lazy as Suresh' and 'Suresh is the laziest boy in the class'.
grammar.30: 'Plant' is a noun when it names a living organism and a verb when it names the action of putting a plant in the soil.

The twentieth century was called the 'Era of the Book' because books were an important means of recording, preserving and spreading knowledge and ideas. They played a major role in human intellectual and cultural life.

The postmaster was deeply moved by Lencho's faith in God. He collected money from his employees and friends and contributed part of his own salary. He sent the money to Lencho in an envelope signed 'God' so that Lencho's faith would remain strong.
Valli avoided friendship with the elderly woman because she found her appearance and manner unpleasant. She valued her independence and did not want to talk to someone she did not like.
After arriving, the fog sits silently over the harbour and city like a cat. It stays for a while and then moves away quietly.
Tricki's belongings included his favourite cushion and toys and other comforts from home. Mrs Pumphrey also sent his food and medicines because she was extremely worried about his health.
Griffin escaped without being seen by removing his clothes and becoming completely invisible. He then slipped away unnoticed while the people around him could not see him.

Richard Ebright was curious, hardworking, disciplined and eager to learn. He observed carefully, carried out experiments and took science seriously. His mother encouraged reading, observation and scientific work. These qualities helped him develop into a successful scientist.

Bishamber Nath arrived with a large marriage party and appeared prosperous. During the ceremony he demanded five thousand rupees as dowry. Bholi refused to marry him because she understood that he was greedy and disrespectful. OR The Historian concludes that ordinary books and nursery rhymes defeated the Martians. The pilot entered a storm, lost visibility and found that his compass and radio had stopped working. He became lost and was running short of fuel. A mysterious black aeroplane appeared and guided him through the clouds. After landing, the control tower said that no other plane had been seen. OR Chubukov is a wealthy landowner and Natalya's father. He is short-tempered, argumentative and quarrelsome. He argues about Oxen Meadows and the dogs and adds to the comedy of the play. At the same time, he wants Natalya to marry Lomov.

Anne came from a loving Jewish family. Her father Otto Frank was caring and understanding, while her mother Edith was affectionate though Anne sometimes felt less close to her. Anne had an elder sister, Margot. The family went into hiding because of Nazi persecution. Anne was especially attached to her father. Her diary became the place where she expressed her thoughts and feelings.

The pader was an important traditional baker in Goa. He supplied bread and sweet breads for daily meals, festivals, marriages and other occasions. His bamboo staff announced his arrival. Children eagerly waited for bread-bangles. The baking profession was respected and continued through generations.

The tiger in the zoo is confined behind bars and cannot roam freely. It walks angrily along the cage and ignores the visitors. At night it hears the sound of patrolling cars instead of jungle sounds. In the wild it would hunt and move through the forest according to its instincts. The poem shows the sadness of captivity and the loss of natural freedom.

Belinda appears timid at first, but she proves courageous when danger arrives. When the pirate threatens the group, she faces the situation and calls for help. Her courage contrasts with the earlier boasting of the other characters. The poem humorously shows that real bravery is revealed in a crisis.

Matilda is unhappy because she dreams of luxury and high social status. She does not value the modest comforts available to her and constantly compares herself with richer people. Her dissatisfaction makes her miserable. The story teaches that we should value what we have instead of allowing envy to control us.

Source: 'The Ball Poem' — Poet: John Berryman. Context: The speaker describes a fresh moonlit night while the boy is experiencing the pain of losing his ball. The peaceful setting contrasts with his emotional loss and supports the poem's lesson about growing up.

Source: 'For Anne Gregory' — Poet: W. B. Yeats. Context: Anne Gregory says that she can change the colour of her hair with dye. The statement occurs in a discussion about physical beauty and whether people can love a person for inner qualities rather than outward appearance.

The young seagull is initially afraid that his wings will not support him. Hunger finally overcomes his fear when his mother tempts him with a piece of fish. He jumps towards the food, spreads his wings and discovers that he can fly. He then flies confidently towards his family. OR Kodagu/Coorg is a beautiful hill region with evergreen forests, coffee plantations, streams and the Brahmagiri hills. Its pleasant climate, wildlife and natural scenery make it attractive. The region also offers adventure activities and rich cultural traditions.

Buddha explains that human life is troubled because birth, old age, disease, death and separation are unavoidable. Suffering is increased by attachment and desire. Kisa Gotami learns this when every house she visits has experienced death. She understands that mortality is universal. OR Mandela says every person has twin obligations: one to family and another to the community and country. Under apartheid he could not fulfil both freely, so he sacrificed personal freedom to fight for the freedom of his people.

'Dust of Snow' shows that a small natural incident can change a person's mood. A crow shakes snow from a hemlock tree onto the poet. Although both the crow and hemlock normally have negative associations, the incident refreshes him and saves part of a day he had regretted. OR The boy is upset because the lost ball has emotional value and memories attached to it. Another ball may cost little, but it cannot replace the personal experience represented by the lost ball. The loss teaches him about responsibility and accepting the realities of life.

a) Modern propaganda and war are major threats to democracy. Propaganda can suppress opposing views and weaken people's judgement, while war creates a mentality in which democratic methods become difficult. b) Democracy depends on constant access to facts, honest public discussion, economic security and welfare, and a kindly and cooperative outlook among citizens.

TV – A source of information for youth: Television can be a useful source of information for young people. News programmes help them understand events in their country and the world. Educational channels can explain science, history, geography and current affairs. Documentaries introduce students to people, places and cultures. Interviews and discussions can develop awareness of social issues. Television can also improve language and general knowledge. However, all programmes are not equally useful. Excessive entertainment can waste valuable study time. Some programmes may contain misleading or unsuitable information. Young viewers should therefore choose programmes carefully. Parents and teachers can guide them. Television should be used in moderation. It should support reading and study rather than replace them. With responsible viewing, television can broaden the knowledge of youth. OR Restore Natural Resources for Future generations: Natural resources such as water, forests, soil, minerals and wildlife are essential for life. Rapid population growth and careless development are putting these resources under pressure. Deforestation causes soil erosion and loss of wildlife. Pollution makes water and air unsafe. Overuse of groundwater and minerals creates further problems. We should plant trees and protect forests. Water must be conserved and rainwater harvested. Waste should be reduced, reused and recycled. Renewable sources of energy should be encouraged. Farmers should use soil and water responsibly. Governments must enforce environmental laws. Communities can restore lakes and protect local ecosystems. Students can save water, avoid plastic and spread awareness. Restoring resources is our duty to future generations. Sustainable use today will protect life tomorrow.

I shall be grateful for your consideration. Yours obediently, Gita/Gayan.

The lady deceived Horace by pretending to be the owner of the house. She claimed that she had forgotten the safe combination and persuaded him to open it for her. She then took the jewels and left, while Horace was later caught by the police.

Ebright's mother encouraged him by providing books, scientific materials and opportunities to learn. She took his interests seriously, encouraged experiments and helped him develop the habit of reading and observing. Her support played a major role in his success.

Bholi finds her teacher different because the teacher treats her with kindness and patience instead of mocking her. She encourages Bholi to speak without fear and assures her that education will make her confident. At home, people had neglected or ridiculed her.

M. and Mme Loisel replaced the lost necklace by borrowing money and buying a similar necklace. They spent ten years working hard and living in poverty to repay the debt. Later they learned that the original necklace had been an imitation and was not worth much.

The hailstorm completely destroyed Lencho's field. The hailstones fell heavily and covered the crop like a blanket. Not a single crop was left. The corn and flowers were ruined. The trees were stripped of leaves and branches. Lencho's hope of a good harvest disappeared in a few minutes. He was left helpless and deeply disappointed.

Nelson Mandela struggled against apartheid, a system that denied black people political and social equality. He joined the African National Congress and opposed racial discrimination. He was imprisoned for many years because of his resistance. Even in prison he remained committed to freedom and equality. He believed that both the oppressed and the oppressor needed freedom. His struggle eventually contributed to the end of apartheid. He became South Africa's first black President in a democratic government.

The poem shows that a negative-looking incident can have a positive effect. A crow shakes snow from a hemlock tree onto the poet. The crow and hemlock usually suggest unpleasantness, yet the falling snow changes the poet's mood. He realises that the remaining part of his day need not be wasted. Thus a small negative-looking event produces a positive result.

The poet uses humour, exaggeration and playful descriptions to identify dangerous animals. The lion roars, the tiger may eat a person, the leopard springs, the bear hugs, the hyena laughs and the crocodile sheds tears. The poem gives absurdly cheerful advice about dangerous situations. The contrast between danger and humour makes the poem entertaining.

Hari Singh did understand the value of education, although he understood it gradually. At first he stole Anil's money because he wanted quick gain. Later he remembered that Anil could teach him to read and write. He realised that education could change his future. He returned the stolen money because he did not want to lose this opportunity. His decision shows that he valued education more than temporary wealth.

The Proposal is full of quarrels between Lomov, Natalya and Chubukov. Lomov comes to propose to Natalya but begins arguing about Oxen Meadows. He then quarrels with her about the superiority of their dogs, Guess and Squeezer. Chubukov joins the arguments instead of calming them. The characters repeatedly insult one another and forget the purpose of Lomov's visit. Their temper and stubbornness create humour. The play shows how petty quarrels can dominate important matters. OR Valli's enthusiasm was dampened when she saw a cow lying dead by the roadside on her return journey. Earlier she had enjoyed watching the same lively cow running beside the bus. Seeing it dead shocked and saddened her. The sight changed her cheerful mood. It made her realise that life can change suddenly. The incident made her return journey much less enjoyable.

Source: 'The Black Aeroplane' — Author: Frederick Forsyth. Context: The pilot has entered a dangerous storm and is worried about reaching home. He follows the mysterious black aeroplane through the clouds and hopes to land safely in time for breakfast. The line shows his hopeful attitude during the difficult flight.

Source: 'From the Diary of Anne Frank' — Author: Anne Frank. Context: Anne and her classmates are waiting anxiously for the results. Her friends repeatedly say, 'You're going to pass' while she is still uncertain, especially about mathematics. The line shows the nervous excitement before the results.

Source: 'A Tiger in the Zoo' — Poet: Leslie Norris. Context: The tiger is trapped in a cage and cannot use its natural strength and freedom. The line contrasts the tiger's physical power with its helpless condition behind bars. The poem criticises captivity and expresses sympathy for the animal.

Source: 'The Ball Poem' — Poet: John Berryman. Context: The poet explains that the boy's lost ball has personal and emotional value. A replacement ball is inexpensive, but the boy is learning that some losses cannot simply be replaced. The line begins the lesson about accepting loss and responsibility.

Mijbil caused great confusion when he escaped from the box in the aeroplane. He ran along the aisle and passengers became frightened and curious. He disappeared among the seats and the pilot and passengers had difficulty catching him. His energetic movements created a noisy and comic situation. Eventually Maxwell managed to control him. The incident shows Mijbil's playful nature and makes the journey humorous. OR Anne felt lonely despite having loving parents and many friends because she did not feel that she had a true friend with whom she could share her deepest thoughts. She wanted someone who would listen patiently and understand her feelings. She therefore treated her diary as a friend and called it Kitty. Her loneliness was emotional rather than physical.

Coorg is called a piece of heaven because of its beautiful geographical features. It is a small hill region in Karnataka surrounded by misty hills and evergreen forests. Coffee plantations cover large areas. The region has the Brahmagiri hills and the river Kaveri. Its pleasant climate and rich wildlife make it attractive. The forests contain many plants, birds and animals. The landscape is ideal for trekking and other outdoor activities. These natural features give Coorg its heavenly beauty. OR Buddha taught that life is temporary and full of suffering. Birth, old age, illness and death are unavoidable. Human attachment to worldly things causes sorrow. Kisa Gotami learns that death visits every family. Buddha teaches acceptance of mortality and the need to overcome attachment. Peace comes from understanding the truth of life. His teaching helps people face suffering with wisdom and detachment.

The poem 'The Trees' presents a conflict between human control and nature's desire for freedom. The trees are shown as being confined inside a house and struggling to move out into the open. The poet imagines their branches, roots and leaves working towards freedom. Human beings have tried to control nature, but nature cannot remain confined forever. The movement of the trees symbolises the return of nature to its natural place. The poem therefore presents freedom as a powerful force. OR It is not right to judge a person only by physical appearance. In 'For Anne Gregory', Anne's beautiful hair attracts human attention, but the poem questions whether such attraction is genuine love. Physical beauty can change, while inner qualities are more lasting. The poem suggests that human beings often notice outward appearance first. Only God can love a person for the inner self alone. Therefore true judgement should consider character and inner beauty rather than appearance.

Ban Plastics – Save Environment: Plastic is useful but its careless use has become a serious environmental problem. Plastic bags and packaging are thrown into streets, drains, rivers and fields. They do not decompose easily and remain in the environment for many years. Plastic waste can block drains and cause flooding. Animals may eat plastic and become sick or die. Plastic pollution also harms rivers, oceans and soil. We should reduce the use of single-use plastic. Cloth and reusable bags are better alternatives. Shops and consumers should avoid unnecessary plastic packaging. Plastic waste should be collected and recycled properly. Schools can organise awareness programmes and clean-up drives. Governments should enforce effective waste-management rules. Every citizen must use plastic responsibly. Small changes in daily habits can reduce pollution. Saving the environment requires collective action. Therefore, we should say no to unnecessary plastic and protect nature for future generations. OR Manners Maketh a Man: Good manners make a person pleasant, respectful and responsible. A well-mannered person speaks politely and listens to others. Good manners show consideration for people's feelings. Saying please, thank you and sorry costs nothing but creates goodwill. We should respect elders, teachers, workers and people of every background. Good manners are important at home, school and in public places. We should wait for our turn and avoid disturbing others. Clean habits and proper behaviour are also signs of good manners. A person's education is incomplete without good character. Manners help us build healthy relationships. They also create a peaceful society. Rudeness may hurt others and damage relationships. Children should learn manners from family and school. Good manners should become a natural part of daily life. They reflect discipline, kindness and self-respect. Therefore, manners truly help make a person a better human being.
